content: Lamium album, commonly known as White Deadnettle, is a flowering plant that belongs to the family Lamiaceae. It is native to Europe and western Asia and thrives in a variety of habitats, including open grasslands and woodlands, typically on moist and fertile soils. This plant is a herbaceous perennial that grows to a height of 50 to 100 cm. Its stems are green and have a characteristic four-angled shape. They are triangular in shape with a rounded base, covered in soft hairs, and have serrated edges. Each leaf is attached to the stem by a petiole that can be up to 5 cm long. The leaves bear a superficial resemblance to those of the Stinging Nettle (Urtica dioica), but they lack stinging hairs, which is why the plant is referred to as dead nettle. The flowers of White Deadnettle are white in color and are arranged in whorls, also known as verticillasters, along the upper part of the stem. Each individual flower is approximately 1.5 to 2.5 cm in length. The young leaves of Lamium album are edible and can be consumed raw in salads or cooked as a vegetable. The plant is also valued for its applications in herbal medicine. Its flowers are rich in nectar and pollen, making them highly attractive to bees, which has earned the plant the nickname Bee Nettle. Although native to Europe and western Asia, Lamium album has been introduced to North America, where it has become widely naturalized.
